label: gap_ledger
formula: D_max = T_C / (10 * N_calls * t_layer), with N_calls = k*(sigma/e); gap = current per-call T-depth / D_max. Quantum time T_Q = N_calls * depth * t_layer (serial).

definitions.sigma: sigma_Q, sd of the plain (unsmoothed) payoff the oracle computes
definitions.k_eff: controlled Grover calls / (sigma/e); bounded AE is span-normalised ($64) not sigma-normalised, so k_eff ~ 15*pi*64/sigma*rounding

most_favourable_cell: B8x52 at eps=$0.10: gap 1.97e5x at the current certified-style schedule (k_eff~1067, 122,865 calls) and 100 ns; 554x at hypothetical k=3/100 ns; 18.5x even at k=1 and 10 ns. It wins only because classical T_C there (0.414 s, OSS small-n mark at 4,096 points) is dominated by fixed runtime overhead; the C5 per-scramble fit puts marginal compute near 0.18 s and a lean single-process implementation would be far lower, so this cell's gap is an upper-bound-favourable (QF) reading. Among cells with a non-overhead-dominated classical time, B8x52 eps=0.001 (gap 2.3e5 / 1,018 at k=3) is nominally next, but the current B8 source is ineligible there (bias bound $0.00124 > $0.00055 headroom). B4x12 is 4-8x worse than B8x52 at every eps because its classical time is 4-8x smaller while its depth is only 16% smaller.
levers_ranked: 1. Estimator constant k (E02/E03/E04/E08/E09/E14/E21/E24/E25, C05): current k_eff 586-1067 (span $64 normalisation = 11-12x sigma, 15 median repetitions, power-of-2 M rounding up to 1.8x). Plausible closure x30-x300 (variance-normalised estimator x~10, cheaper 99% amplification x2-5, non-dyadic M / 13/20 split x1.5-2); x15 more in latency only by running the 15 repetitions on 15 machine copies (E20, 15x width). Ceiling k=1 is x600-1000. Largest single lever and the cheapest to settle on paper.

2. Per-call oracle depth (A-family, F-family formulations): current 555,774 / 663,704 clean T-depth. Known remaining compile levers ~x10^2 (WHY_NO_ADVANTAGE s6); Gaussian preparation is ~80% of the leaf-score depth (9.0e5 -> 1.8e5 if free, x~4-5); eps-tailored narrower words at eps>=0.03 maybe x1.5-3; hypothetical Chakrabarti-per-operator 9.5e3 would be x70. Plausible x10-x100; x1,000 needs an oracle shallower than one current multiply (11,088).

3. Logical T-layer time t_layer (H01-H18): 100 ns is already 10-100x more optimistic than projected 1-10 us reaction-limited layers; moving to 10 ns gives x10 but is unprojected, and B8 needs ~6,400 T gates per layer (4.27e9 T / 663,704) i.e. ~6e10 magic states/s at 100 ns. Realistic direction is adverse (x10-x100 worse), so this lever cannot be counted on to close gap.

4. Accuracy target within the fixed task: tightening eps 0.01->0.001 improves the B8 gap only ~x5 (classical p_C~1.6 measured: T_C x40.7 vs calls x8) and requires a new more-precise B8 source; loose-eps cells are already overhead-dominated. Plausible <=x5; no further room inside the fixed eps set.

5. Classical comparator T_C (C-family/F-family): every pending correction is adverse to quantum: removing fixed intercepts (x2-x100 at eps>=0.03), C6 GPU g in {1,10,100}, monotone envelope already applied. Closes 0; expected to widen the gap x1-x100.
what_would_have_to_be_true_for_10x: At the most favourable cell (B8x52, eps=$0.10, T_C=0.414 s taken as is) the product k_eff*depth*t_layer must fall ~2e5-fold from today (k_eff 1067, depth 663,704, 100 ns). Combinations that just reach 10x there: (a) k=3 AND a complete clean 8x52 path oracle of <=1,200 T-layers at 100 ns (554x shallower than accepted; ~1/9 of one current range-narrow multiply); (b) k=1 AND depth <=3,600 at 100 ns (185x); (c) k=3, depth <=12,000 (55x) AND sustained 10 ns logical T-layers (with T-count unchanged at 4.3e9 per call this implies ~4e13 magic states/s); (d) k=1, 10 ns and depth <=35,900 (18.5x). Each also requires the classical side to stay at its overhead-dominated laptop time (no GPU, no lean implementation), a 99% certificate at that k, and the open G2/G3/G5 obligations at no extra depth. The plausible lever product with t_layer held at 100 ns (k x30-300 times depth x10-100 = x300-x3e4) does not reach the ~x2e5 needed; reaching 10x needs both levers at the top of their plausible range plus a ~10x faster logical layer than the already-generous 100 ns. At eps=0.001 (B8, only if a new more precise source fits the $0.00055 bias headroom) one would need depth <=652 at k=3/100 ns. Hence 10x anywhere in the fixed task requires simultaneously k~1-3 at 99% (not demonstrated), an oracle 10^2-10^3x shallower than any built, and a 10-100 ns sustained logical layer (projections 1-10 us). No single lever suffices and no combination is supported by current evidence; percent-level certificates (E11 L2 bridges, small A-family depth gains) move the gap by <=1.3x and cannot change this verdict.
data_quality_caveats: MEASURED: sigma_Q (2^20 paths, CI +/-0.2%), A10 accepted source T-depth/T-count, E07/E24/E02 call count 983,025 at eps=0.01 for both B4 and B8, C2/C5 warm wall times (16-core Intel Ultra 7 155H laptop), G2 bias bounds B4<=$0.000205, B8<=$0.00124 (eps=0.01 contract).

MODELLED: call counts at eps 0.10/0.03/0.001 (E07 formula, same span 64 and 15 repetitions; rotation-synthesis certificate for M=524,288 missing as for 131,072); classical T_C for rqmc/oss/oss_bb at eps=0.001 and several eps=0.03 rows are fitted ('modelled all-16'), not executed; k=1/k=3 rows are hypothetical constants, not schedules.

MISSING: per-iterate depth for the A10 source (E02 iterate 571,034/770,356 was on an older source; reflections/marking overhead not re-derived, likely a few %); Clifford depth (~3x T-depth) and reaction-limited scheduling; physical layer time (G5/H03 failed run); C6 GPU timing; C8 out-of-sample; true-price 99% coverage for classical (C4 only fails to detect undercoverage); finite-law classical comparator (classical targets continuous law, quantum finite Box-Muller law).

Classical T_C at eps 0.10/0.03 are 'measured small-n marks' of 64-4,096 points dominated by a 0.16-0.64 s fixed intercept; B8 preint eps=0.01 confirmation (0.554 s) is faster than its own eps=0.03 mark (0.910 s), so a monotone envelope (T_C(eps) <= T_C(tighter eps)) was applied; B8 eps=0.01 confirmation met the half-width in only 55% of runs. All of these inflate T_C and favour quantum.

B8x52 at eps=0.001 is infeasible for the current source: its certified continuous-to-native bias bound ($0.00124) exceeds the 0.55*eps deterministic headroom ($0.00055); the WHY_NO_ADVANTAGE/decision_interim D_max=652 row assumes an eligible source that does not exist.

Bounded AE calls are span-normalised ($64) and independent of sigma; k_eff=calls/(sigma/e) is a derived comparison constant, not the estimator's native parameter. The 13/20 error split (E24) halves calls at eps=0.01 (491,505) but C05 retained the 0.45 split.

Quantum latency counts all calls serially; the 15 repetitions could run on 15 machine copies (longest chain 65,535 calls at eps=0.01), a x15 latency reduction at x15 width (~67M logical qubits for B8), while classical is held to 16 cores.

Older figures differ: WHY_NO_ADVANTAGE s2.5 used T_C=27.1 s (historical) and leaf-score depth 9.0e5 -> D_max 789, gap 1,138; decision_interim_v2 uses T_C=22.53 s and Stage C depths (3.34M clean dependency-only), not the A10 555,774/663,704 used here.
